title: One call to a GPU anywhere
subtitle: Provisioning a GPU consumer node on the workbench, on a LAN host or in the cloud with one tool call, under a daily budget that only a human can set

stats.label: actions on the one provisioning tool
inbound ports for a cloud pod to reach the estate
between budget checks on every container, healthy ones included
the day's budget when no limit row exists

lede: An agent in my estate can stand up a GPU worker with one tool call: a container image, an engine, a provider, and where it should run. The same call starts a container on my workbench over the local socket, on a LAN workstation over mutual TLS, or on a rented cloud pod that dials back into my network with no inbound ports. Before any of that happens, a budget gate checks the day's dollar cap, which is set by a human with a command-line tool that is not on any agent's tool surface. Spend is metered from the second the provider confirms the pod, and a container that outlives the budget is terminated.
quote: Missing or invalid state can only yield zero or an error, never a larger cap.
evidence: Cloud GPU provisioning with cost controls: one tool with 15 actions stands up a GPU worker on the workbench, a LAN host or a rented cloud pod.

Zero-trust and zero-inbound networking: cloud pods dial back through an outbound tunnel, reaching Redis and PostgreSQL with 0 inbound ports; LAN hosts are driven over mutual TLS from a private certificate authority.
Budget enforcement for AI agents: a daily dollar cap set only by a human command-line tool, checked before any side effect, failing closed at $0 when no limit row exists.
Metering and reconciliation: spend accumulated per container, per schema and globally, with health checks every 30 s that terminate any container still up once the budget is spent.
Container runtime design: one host-built runtime binary bind-mounted with a loader into any image, and four loader modes that decide what a container becomes.
author: Corey James
